source: Independent read-only review of the revision-2 brief, spec, plan, test specification, graph, and Architect delta approval.

findings.title: Role vocabulary and approval-mode mapping remain unresolved
evidence: plan.md:209-213 records exact government/financial role names and the mapping of plan-only, prompted, standing-policy, and noninteractive modes to plan/manual/auto/dontAsk/bypassPrompts as UNKNOWN.
test-spec.md:40-42 and 81-89 require stable role identifiers, every mode, and high-risk step-up behavior.
G001 and G004 are the first owners of these contracts, while G002, G005, G008, and G009 consume them.
findings.impact: G001 and G004 must invent public identifiers or mode semantics, and downstream fixtures cannot be stable. This violates the no-replanning/no-invented-API worker requirement.
findings.requiredChange: Freeze the role enum, role-to-risk/release derivation table, and exact five-mode mapping before dispatch. Define whether bypassPrompts is an internal-only escape and how noninteractive execution is represented.

findings.title: Import, compatibility-envelope, and closed-response contracts lack field-level schemas
evidence: spec.md:56-63 names ImportProvenance/ImportResult counts, loss entries, and source identifiers but does not define their fields, enums, requiredness, or closed shape.

spec.md:86-102 describes EncryptedAutofillProfileEnvelope and PadlocBrokerResponse conceptually but does not define serialized fields, error variants, key-wrap/unwrap operations, or exact nested payload schemas.
test-spec.md:38-39, 116-120, and 133-135 require closed deterministic fixtures and rejection of unknown nested keys.
findings.impact: G002, G005, G006, and G008 cannot implement interoperable parsers or deterministic fixtures without choosing APIs and wire shapes themselves. A closed parser cannot be written from only a list of payload categories.
findings.requiredChange: Add exact versioned TypeScript/JSON schemas for ImportResult, loss entries, the encrypted envelope, broker response variants, structured errors, and the one-time key-custody handshake. Name the canonical fixture and transport operations.

findings.title: The privacy-gate matrix omits existing value-bearing observation paths
evidence: test-spec.md:149-164 lists open_snapshot, page text/accessibility, evidence, bridge observation/fetch, screenshots, read_image, links/tables, eval, and network/body capture, but omits document_text, shape, network_detail, replay_request, and form_inspect.
magic-browser/src/worker/typed-tools.ts:104-126 exposes those omitted tools; document_text is implemented at :2456, network_detail/replay_request at :2721-2800, and form_inspect at :2833-2846.
magic-browser/src/runtime/form.ts:14-37 includes FormField.value and :76-107 includes FormActionResult.value, so form inspection/action output is directly value-bearing.
G007 owns typed-tools.ts but not runtime/form.ts, and no test requirement proves these paths block on unknown/potentially-private state.
findings.impact: A worker can satisfy the written G007 tests while leaving direct model-observation/body/form routes open after a private fill, contradicting the brief's all-generic-observation invariant.
findings.requiredChange: Publish an exhaustive observation-tool inventory with gate call sites and exact-target behavior. Add negative tests for document_text, shape, network_detail, replay_request, form_inspect, and any form-action outputs; assign omitted producer files or explicitly document safe exceptions.

findings.title: G009 has no canonical cross-repository runner or clean-state bootstrap
evidence: graph-candidate.json G009 owns two scripts and two fixture trees, one in each repository, but names no canonical entrypoint, invocation command, working-directory contract, or cross-repository handoff.
test-spec.md:184-200 says 'one deterministic script' while also requiring both repository runners, native-host install, browser setup, scanners, cleanup, and a padloc-owned evidence directory.

spec.md:64-79 and :104-113 make unknown privacy state fail closed and make an exact trusted reset the only producer of clean, but test-spec.md:184-188 starts G009 at install/unlock/classify without specifying the reset/clean bootstrap.
findings.impact: G009 must invent orchestration and may be unable to reach classify/plan under the fail-closed unknown state. G010 cannot document an exact command that the plan never names.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one canonical runner and command, define its two-repository invocation and artifact handoff, and add the exact synthetic target-descriptor/reset sequence that establishes clean before the first observation.

findings.title: Proof authority ownership and pass criteria are ambiguous
evidence: plan.md:214-216 allows G008 either to add proof keys or leave closure explicitly incomplete.
graph-candidate.json G008 lists only padloc/.ch5/proof.yaml, while the prepared magic-browser tree has its own .ch5/proof.yaml and no corresponding graph-owned proof file.
test-spec.md:9-11 and :178-180 require exact proof keys and exact-SHA records, but do not name the required command IDs, evidence paths, or which repository is authoritative.
findings.impact: G008/G009/G010 have no deterministic pass/fail boundary and can legally finish with UNKNOWN despite the required evidence outcome. Cross-repository proof may be recorded in the wrong authority.
findings.requiredChange: Declare the owning proof authority, required command keys, exact-SHA/evidence paths, and whether both repositories register lanes. Make missing keys a blocking failure rather than an optional closure state.

findings.title: G008 promises shared fixtures but assigns only two independent test files
evidence: test-spec.md:168-180 requires both repositories to parse the same synthetic role, protocol, privacy, and envelope fixtures.

graph-candidate.json G008 owns padloc/packages/extension/test/agentic-contract-fixtures.ts and magic-browser/src/runtime/agentic-contract-fixtures.test.ts, but no canonical shared fixture artifact, generator, or content hash.
The plan's contract schemas are not field-level (C2), so duplicated fixtures can drift while both local tests pass.
findings.impact: The claimed cross-repository parity proof is not reproducible; each worker can create a different fixture set and still satisfy its local test name.
findings.requiredChange: Assign one canonical synthetic fixture source (or generated artifact with a recorded hash), define the read-only consumer in the other repository, and make parity fail on source/hash drift.

nodeAssessment.cheapestProof: Core round-trip, creation-propagation, and ImportResult contract fixtures
Synthetic relying-party registration/assertion plus binding and stale-verification negatives
Permission-engine/store matrix for every mode, reason, revision, lock, revoke, and step-up case
Broker protocol, privacy ledger/reset, native redaction, and encrypted-envelope negative fixtures
CLI authority cutover plus closed-schema and ciphertext-only transport tests
Shared-gate state matrix plus one negative test per observation primitive
Canonical fixture parity and proof-authority command records
One canonical synthetic runner with leak scanner and redacted evidence
Docs link/command check against the canonical G009 entrypoint

positiveEvidence: Architect delta APPROVE is for the exact revision-2 hashes reviewed here.
Graph JSON parses, is acyclic, has symmetric parallel edges, disjoint declared parallel ownership, and repository-prefixed paths.
The synthetic-only posture, no-working-credential-mutation rule, closed privacy-state intent, and pre-mortem cover the main declared risk classes.
G003 has a bounded file/symbol region, serial handoff, and an executable synthetic proof shape once shared contracts are frozen.
rationale: Revision 2 repairs Architect findings A1-A9 and is structurally sound, but it still leaves product-contract decisions and acceptance boundaries explicitly UNKNOWN. The omitted value-bearing observation paths and unspecified cross-repository runner/proof authority are blocking executability and security coverage gaps. Iterate the plan/spec/test/graph contracts before implementation dispatch; do not reject the overall architecture.
nextGate: Plan correction must resolve C1-C6, rerun graph and contract validation, then obtain a fresh independent Architect review before worker dispatch.
